## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Piṭṭhiduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 21.16) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka. Structurally, the text investigates conditional relations by cross-combining categories of the Piṭṭhiduka (supplementary or "back" dyads) with the Kusalattika (the triad of wholesome, unwholesome, and undetermined phenomena) within the *Paṭṭhāna* analytical matrix. No specific modern English translations, individual commentaries, or independent secondary literature discussions are preserved in the dossier for this specific leaf section.

Text-reuse calculations by DharmaNexus demonstrate extensive formulaic repetition characteristic of the *Paṭṭhāna*, finding 1,671 matching passages shared between Patthana 21.16 and 185 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its highest levels of text sharing occur with structurally corresponding or adjacent sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, particularly another treatment of *Piṭṭhiduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.13; 105 matches, including segment range §1.1–3.1_1 aligned with §1.1–6.1), *Mahantaraduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 21.13; 77 matches), and *Cūḷantaraduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 21.5; 42 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial segments are likewise shared with *Tika Kusalattika* (Patthana 5.2) and *Kusalattika, Tika* (Patthana 5.1) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns several brief passages with Tibetan translations of Sanskrit Abhidharma works, specifically the *Abhidharmakośakārikā* (D4089) and the *Abhidharmakoṣabhāṣyaṭīkātattvārtha* (D4421), though these reflect low-scoring machine-generated terminological correspondences rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
